About Eppix Labs · Canadian research peptide supplier

Every Lot Tested. Every Result Published, Exactly as Measured.

Eppix Labs supplies research peptides across Canada from Canadian stock. We were built on one rule: if a purity number is on the label, the independent lab report behind it is published against that lot, where anyone can check it.

What Eppix Labs Does

We stock research peptides in Canada for laboratories and researchers and ship them by Canada Post Xpresspost, same day before 4 pm. Every compound in the catalog is supplied for in vitro and laboratory research purposes only — we provide no dosing, administration or protocol guidance, and nothing on this site describes what a compound does in humans.

What makes us different is not the catalog; several Canadian suppliers stock similar compounds. It is that every lot we sell has an independent laboratory report — Janoshik Analytical for almost every lot; HPLC purity and mass-spec identity — published in full on our certificate library, matched to the lot number printed on the vial, and linked to the same result on the lab’s own portal.

Why It Matters

A purity percentage tells you what fraction of the material in a vial is the compound on the label. It says nothing about how much material is there. A vial can be highly pure and still short-filled. That is why we publish two numbers for every lot: HPLC purity and measured content in milligrams against the label claim.

We don’t publish purity figures we haven’t tested for, and we never reuse a certificate from a previous batch on new stock. If a lot number isn’t in our library, it didn’t come from us.

The Eppix Verification Standard

  1. Step 01 · Before release

    Independent lab analysis

    Each lot is sent to an independent laboratory after fill — Janoshik Analytical for almost every lot. The lab runs HPLC for purity and mass spectrometry for identity, and reports the milligrams actually found in the vial. On batches chosen at random we commission further screening on top of that: heavy metals, sterility and bacterial endotoxin, published on the lots they were run on.

    Latest lot — Lot TESA-CA-26I-20 · HPLC 99.273% · 21.98 mg / 20 mg

  2. Step 02 · The result

    Published as measured

    Most lots measure above 99% HPLC purity. A few compounds are harder to make and come back in the high 98s — those results are published too, in the same library, rather than left out of the average.

    Mean across all 69 lots: 99.47% HPLC purity · lowest 97.65%

  3. Step 03 · Published

    Certificate matched to the vial

    The full report is published on our certificate library under the lot number printed on the label, with a link to the same report on verify.janoshik.com. No PDF-only, no summaries.

    /certificates-of-analysis/verify

What We Stand For

  1. 01

    Independent, not in-house. Every result comes from a third-party laboratory — Janoshik Analytical for almost every lot. We do not self-certify.

  2. 02

    Batch-specific, always. Every product carries a lot number before distribution, and that lot maps to exactly one certificate.

  3. 03

    Publicly linked, not PDF-only. Any researcher can verify a batch directly with the issuing laboratory without contacting us.

  4. 04

    Research use only, without exception. No dosing, no administration, no claims about effects in humans — on the site, in support, or in ads.

  5. 05

    Canadian stock, Canadian delivery. Orders ship within Canada by Canada Post Xpresspost with tracking, free over $200.
